school.title: Parent-teacher meeting
school.summary: Know what happens in a school conference, who attends, and what questions to bring.

whatHappens.title: What will happen
whatHappens.body: You will sit with the teacher to hear how your child is doing in class, see recent schoolwork, and agree on one or two next steps. You can ask the teacher to slow down or explain any school term.
whatHappens.tip: Your teenager can sit beside you to help track notes, while you lead the talk.

whoIsThere.title: Who will be there
whoIsThere.body: Usually your child's teacher, you, and sometimes a school counselor or a professional interpreter if requested ahead of time. You are the parent and decision-maker.
whoIsThere.tip: Your child is your supporter, not the interpreter for sensitive or official school topics.

howLong.title: How long it takes
howLong.body: Most parent-teacher meetings last 15 to 20 minutes. Arrive 10 minutes early to find the classroom or sign in at the front office.
howLong.tip: If you need more time, you can ask to schedule a follow-up talk.

whatToBring.title: What to bring
whatToBring.body: Bring the items below so you do not have to search at the desk.
items: The meeting invite letter or note
Two questions you want to ask
Your interpreter request card (on your phone or printed)

questions.q1: What is my child doing well in right now?
questions.q2: Where does my child need extra support?
questions.q3: What can we practice at home for 15 minutes a day?
questions.q4: Who should I contact if I have a question later?
questions.q5: Can you send important notes home in my language?

clinic.title: Clinic visit (preparation only)
clinic.summary: Prepare for check-in, paperwork, and asking for an interpreter—no medical advice.
clinic.disclaimer: This guide covers visit preparation and communication rights only. It does not give medical advice.

whatHappens.title: What will happen
whatHappens.body: First, you check in at the front desk and confirm your name and address. Next, a staff member calls you in for basic intake questions before you speak with the clinician.
whatHappens.tip: You can ask for a professional medical interpreter at check-in so nothing is misunderstood.

whoIsThere.title: Who will be there
whoIsThere.body: Front-desk staff, a nurse or medical assistant, the doctor or nurse practitioner, and a professional interpreter (in person, by phone, or by video).
whoIsThere.tip: Your child should never have to translate health conversations. Ask for a trained interpreter.

howLong.title: How long it takes
howLong.body: Plan for 45 to 60 minutes total, including waiting time and check-out paperwork. Arrive 15 minutes early if you are filling out forms for the first time.
howLong.tip: Ask for written instructions before you leave the room.

whatToBring.title: What to bring
whatToBring.body: Pack these documents before you leave home.
items: Insurance card or clinic card (if you have one)
Names or photos of any current medicine bottles

questions.q1: May I have a professional interpreter for this visit?
questions.q2: Can you please write down the next steps clearly?
questions.q3: When and where is my follow-up appointment?
questions.q4: Which phone number should I call if I have a question about paperwork?
questions.q5: Are these forms available in my language?

bank.title: Bank or official letter
bank.summary: Prepare for bank appointments, government offices, or confusing mail without guessing.

whatHappens.title: What will happen
whatHappens.body: A clerk or advisor will check your identity, read your letter or account details, and explain what action or document is needed. Never sign a paper you do not understand.
whatHappens.tip: It is completely normal to say: I want to take this home to read carefully first.

whoIsThere.title: Who will be there
whoIsThere.body: A front-desk greeter, a bank representative or caseworker, and a language interpreter by phone or in person if available.
whoIsThere.tip: Your teen helper can help keep your papers in order, while you speak with the staff and approve decisions.

howLong.title: How long it takes
howLong.body: Allow 30 to 45 minutes. If you do not have an appointment, waiting times can be longer—morning hours are often quieter.
howLong.tip: Ask for a printed receipt or reference number before leaving.

whatToBring.title: What to bring
whatToBring.body: Keep important letters and IDs together in one folder.
items: The official letter and its envelope
Proof of address (a recent utility bill or lease)

questions.q1: What is the exact deadline on this letter?
questions.q2: Which documents do I still need to bring?
questions.q3: Can I take a copy home to review before I sign?
questions.q4: Can you write down my confirmation or reference number?
questions.q5: Is there a fee or penalty I should know about?

interpreterCard.rightsHeading: About your right to an interpreter
interpreterCard.rightsBody: Rules for free professional interpreters vary by country, region, and type of office (schools, public clinics, hospitals, or banks). In many places, public schools and health services must provide an interpreter at no cost.
